fig01.title: Sample Image for SaBaTech: A Banana Fruit Pest and Disease Detection Web Application
fig01.desc: Reference system screenshot — a Philippine web-based, ground-level banana pest and disease detector using a TensorFlow/Keras CNN with ESP32-CAM capture.

fig02.title: Sample Image for GeoDLS: A Deep Learning-Based Corn Disease Tracking and Location System Using RTK Geolocated UAS Imagery
fig02.desc: Reference system — georeferenced corn disease tracking that geolocates diseased regions at GPS coordinates from RTK UAS imagery.

fig03.title: Agile Software Development Methodology
fig03.desc: The iterative Agile/SDLC cycle adopted for AgriVision: Planning, Analysis, Design, Development, Testing, and Maintenance.

fig04.title: Chart of the Project Development Team
fig04.desc: Team organization and accountability structure, led by the Project Adviser over Project Manager, System Architect, Designer, and Developer.

fig05.title: Work Breakdown Structure of AgriVision
fig05.desc: AgriVision decomposed into twelve manageable phases and their measurable work packages.

fig06.title: Gantt Chart of AgriVision
fig06.desc: Master project schedule (March–July 2026) with phase-based color coding and task dependencies.

fig07a.title: Conceptual Framework — Input · Process · Output (IPO) Model
fig07a.desc: High-level abstraction of the system's data flow from drone/GPS input, through preprocessing, YOLOv8 detection, classification and geotagging, to detection results, geotagged locations, heatmaps and reports.

fig07b.title: Conceptual Framework — AgriVision Simulation Framework
fig07b.desc: Step-by-step operational pipeline of the system, detailing the simulation-based development and evaluation flow.

fig08.title: Use Case Diagram of AgriVision
fig08.desc: Interactions between the Drone Pilot and the system: connect feed, start/stop detection, monitor results, set GPS, and capture/export reports.

fig09.title: Context Flow Diagram (Level 0) of AgriVision
fig09.desc: The Pilot provides the casted drone feed; AgriVision analyzes it with YOLOv8 and heatmap generation, returns visual results, and stores processed data in the Dataset.

fig10.title: Level 1 Data Flow Diagram of AgriVision
fig10.desc: Decomposition of the context process: Screen Cast → YOLOv8 Model → Dataset store + Generate Heatmap → visual overlays back to the Pilot.

fig11.title: Entity Relationship Diagram (JSON Schema) of AgriVision
fig11.desc: Logical data objects: VideoSource → Frame → AnalysisResult, linked with GeoTag/GeoMarker to build the LiveMap, compiled into a FieldReport with stored Artifacts.

fig12.title: YOLOv8n AdamW Optimizer — Model Accuracy and Loss
fig12.desc: Training accuracy and loss curves at increasing epoch checkpoints (20, 40, 60, 80). Rising training accuracy against a flatter validation curve indicates overfitting driven by class imbalance.
